name: Soave harvest-site closure
question: Is leaving the inner-cheek buccal graft harvest site open noninferior to closing it for oral pain after substitution urethroplasty?

design.blinding: Allocation concealed until buccal graft harvest; postoperative blinding not stated
design.population: 135 men with urethral stricture analyzed after unilateral buccal harvest for single-stage substitution urethroplasty; 163 consented and 28 were excluded after intraoperative changes.
design.description: Randomized noninferiority trial of cheek donor-site management performed by six reconstructive surgeons
design.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 2–3; Results, p 3; Table 1

verdictNote: Intensity and affective pain met noninferiority throughout; sensory and total pain only at day 21 and month 3.
takeaway: In 135 analyzed men after unilateral buccal graft urethroplasty, donor-site nonclosure was noninferior to closure for oral pain intensity and affective quality at all five postoperative assessments; sensory and total pain met noninferiority only at day 21 and month 3.

reports.label: Primary randomized report
reports.citation: Soave A, Dahlem R, Pinnschmidt HO, et al. "Substitution Urethroplasty with Closure Versus Nonclosure of the Buccal Mucosa Graft Harvest Site: A Randomized Controlled Trial with a Detailed Analysis of Oral Pain and Morbidity." *Eur Urol.* 2018;73(6):910-922. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2017.11.014

results.measure: 11-point numeric rating scale; model-estimated nonclosure-minus-closure difference at postoperative days 1, 5, and 21 and months 3 and 6; one-point noninferiority margin
results.note: Noninferior at all five time points. Figure 1 plots model-estimated means, differences, and 95% confidence intervals without numeric labels in the supplied text; supplementary mean scores are absent.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, Statistical analysis, p 3; Results, p 3; Fig. 1, p 5

results.measure: Short-Form McGill affective pain index; model-estimated nonclosure-minus-closure difference at postoperative days 1, 5, and 21 and months 3 and 6; one-point noninferiority margin
results.note: Noninferior at all five time points. Figure 2 plots model-estimated means, differences, and 95% confidence intervals without numeric labels in the supplied text; supplementary mean scores are absent.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, Statistical analysis, p 3; Results, pp 3–4; Fig. 2, p 6

results.measure: Short-Form McGill sensory pain index; noninferiority of nonclosure versus closure at postoperative days 1, 5, and 21 and months 3 and 6
results.note: Noninferiority met at day 21 and month 3, but not at days 1 or 5 or month 6; Figure 2 gives graphical differences and 95% confidence intervals without numeric labels in the supplied text.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 4; Fig. 2, p 6

results.measure: Short-Form McGill total pain index; noninferiority of nonclosure versus closure at postoperative days 1, 5, and 21 and months 3 and 6
results.note: Noninferiority met at day 21 and month 3, but not at days 1 or 5 or month 6; Figure 2 gives graphical differences and 95% confidence intervals without numeric labels in the supplied text.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 4; Fig. 2, p 6

results.endpoint: Time from urethroplasty and oral pain
results.measure: Covariate effect of postoperative time on pain intensity and sensory, affective, and total pain quality
results.note: Mixed-model covariate analysis; oral pain intensity and sensory, affective, and total pain indices declined over time; no prespecified noninferiority test for this covariate.
results.locator: Full text, Results, pp 3–4; Discussion, pp 4–6

results.measure: Association of graft length with pain intensity and sensory and total pain quality
results.note: Mixed-model covariate analysis; each additional millimeter of graft length corresponded to a 1.014-fold oral-pain intensity NRS score; no prespecified noninferiority test for this covariate.
results.locator: Full text, Results, pp 3–4; Discussion, p 4

harms.label: Oral donor-site morbidity

values.exp: At month 6, numbness 30/42 and impaired mouth opening 14/41 questionnaire respondents
values.ctl: At month 6, numbness 24/42 and impaired mouth opening 20/42 questionnaire respondents

harms.locator: Full text, Table 2, pp 7–8; Results, p 4
harms.note: Other measured domains were bleeding, swelling, altered salivation and taste, and impaired smiling, whistling, diet, and speech. Oral morbidity questions were nonvalidated; group-by-time effects were not significant. Up to 52/135 (39%) lacked a month-6 response for some domains.

harms.label: Oral complications, Clavien-Dindo grade I
harms.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 12; Discussion, p 12
harms.note: Only grade I complications were observed: pain or swelling requiring medication, or bleeding requiring compression; interaction P greater than 0.9. Denominators are reconstructed from table counts, rounded percentages, and total missing responses.

delivery.label: Enrollment period
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, Patient cohort, p 2

delivery.label: Donor-site intervention

values.exp: Inner-cheek harvest site left open after bipolar hemostasis (72 analyzed men)
values.ctl: Inner-cheek harvest site closed with interrupted 4-0 monofilament sutures after bipolar hemostasis (63 analyzed men)

delivery.note: Both groups received temporary cottonoid gauze, daily chamomile rinses, and cheek cooling on postoperative days 1–5.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, Surgical procedure and randomization; Postoperative management, p 2

delivery.label: Analysis set after intraoperative changes
delivery.value: 163 consented; 28 excluded after intraoperative changes (25 two-stage urethroplasties, 3 bilateral harvests); 135 analyzed (72 nonclosure, 63 closure), without an intention-to-treat analysis
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, Patient cohort, p 2; Results, Patients' baseline characteristics, p 3

delivery.label: Graft harvest dimensions
delivery.value: Ovoid inner-cheek grafts, uniformly 15 mm wide; median length 45 mm (quartiles 40–60) in nonclosure and 50 mm (50–80) in closure; 2% lidocaine with adrenaline infiltration
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, Surgical procedure and randomization, p 2; Table 1, p 4

delivery.label: Patient-reported assessment schedule
delivery.value: Before surgery; postoperative days 1, 5, and 21; months 3 and 6
